analysis.title: Morgan Stanley Research: Key Forecasts (Next 12-Months Outlook: Our High-Conviction Calls)
key_insights: Morgan Stanley expects resilient US growth supported by consumption and AI-driven capital spending. Unemployment stays below 4.5%, and higher energy prices keep inflation elevated for longer.

Fed call: two more hikes, in December and March, taking the policy rate to 4.25-4.50% by 1Q27. The bank then expects a hold through 2027 and easing from 2Q28, with the rate reaching 3.625% by end-2028.

ECB: 25bp hikes in December and March to 3.00%, a hold until June 2028, then quarterly cuts. Euro area headline inflation is expected to peak above 4% in early 2027, with core above target until mid-2028.
BoJ: two hikes (December and March) taking the policy rate to 1.75% in March 2027. BoE: another hike in February, then a hold through 2027 and easing in 2028.

Asset allocation: maximum overweight global stocks, equal-weight core fixed income, underweight other fixed income, commodities and cash. Equities are added in every region, and Japan and Europe move to overweight.
The bank closes its underweight in IG corporate credit because the repricing has already occurred. It funds the changes by paring risk in the rest of fixed income, commodities and cash.

Equities: overweight US, Japan and Europe, equal-weight EM. US earnings growth is expected to be mid-teens, driven by operating leverage, steadier rate and oil volatility, and continued AI investment.
Japan: earnings growth slows as AI investment tapers, with banks taking over as the EPS driver as rates normalize. A sharper correction in AI capex is named as the key downside risk.

Europe: the new end-2027 MSCI Europe target implies +15% upside, slightly ahead of the US in total return terms (+19% vs +16%). MSCI Europe has slightly outperformed the S&P 500 since November 2024, and buyback yield is ahead of the US for the first time.

Rates and FX: 10y UST peaks at 5.05% in 2Q27 and ends 2027 at 5.00%. The bank sees modest USD strength, with DXY at 105, EUR/USD at 1.08 ahead of the French presidential election, USD/JPY at 162 and GBP/USD at 1.27. Most value in gilts and Bunds.
Oil: Brent stays at $100/bbl in 1Q27 and returns to $75/bbl by 4Q27. Physical conditions are softening, but flat price remains dependent on geopolitics.
European gas: storage is at a record low for early November (69%) and Qatar LNG flow is 40% of pre-war levels. TTF is forecast at about 90 EUR/MWh in a mild winter, with risks skewed up.

Metals: gold faces headwinds from dollar strength and higher rate expectations. Copper availability is tight near term with US tariff policy the key uncertainty. Aluminium faces a meaningful 2027 surplus.
Credit: prefers IG to sub-IG and US loans over HY bonds. Wider outcome range for sub-IG, partly from competition for capital from chip financing deals.
Global growth forecasts: GDP 4Q/4Q of 3.5% in 2026, 3.3% in 2027 and 3.4% in 2028. US inflation is 3.9% in 2026 before falling to 2.1% in 2027.

sector_views.rationale: Risk assets have cheapened and the AI capex cycle is intact, so earnings growth should extend into 2027. The bank leans into quality cyclicals.
Held at equal-weight as a hedge against long tails.
The underweight is closed because the repricing has already occurred.

earnings_insights: US earnings growth expected to be mid-teens, per the bank's top-down forecast. MS top-down EPS growth forecasts are S&P 500 +14% for 2027, MSCI Europe +8%, Topix +13% and MSCI EM +17%.

Japan earnings growth is expected to slow gradually as AI investment growth tapers, centred on Electric Appliances and Precision Instruments. Banks become a key EPS driver as interest rates normalize.

risk_factors: A sharper correction in AI capex, named as the key downside risk to equities.
Energy prices staying high, which would keep inflation elevated and the Fed, ECB and BoE hiking.
Tails remain long, so the bank pairs risk with quality and keeps bonds as a hedge.
Geopolitics-dependent oil flat price and Middle East uncertainty.
US tariff policy, especially for copper.
Wider range of outcomes for sub-IG credit, and higher rates for lower-rated borrowers.
vol_and_positioning: The US equity view relies on stabilizing rate and oil volatility.
MS continues to anticipate above-average volatility in EM and Japan equities.
The bank recommends keeping bonds as a hedge because tails remain long.
geopolitical: Middle East: the US elections outcome makes a resolution more likely but not imminent, and more Middle East oil is reaching the market.
Qatar LNG flow is at only 40% of pre-war levels, keeping Europe competing for gas supply.
French presidential election is cited as a USD/EUR event risk, with EUR/USD declining to 1.08 ahead of it.
US tariff policy is named as the key uncertainty for copper.

tension_points.bear_case: A sharper correction in AI capex is the key downside risk to equities, especially Japan, where AI investment growth is already tapering.
